name: http_get

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to fetch: `https://...` or `http://...`. On DuckDB 2.0 other schemes, URLs without a host, and URLs with spaces or control characters are rejected; `user:password@` in the URL is sent as basic auth.

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Optional request headers as a [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map), e.g. `MAP{'accept': 'application/json'}`. Names and values containing line breaks are rejected. On DuckDB 2.0 the parameter can be left out (`NULL` means no headers).

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Optional query parameters. Each entry is percent-encoded and appended to the URL's query string (with `&` if the URL already has one).

returns: A JSON object with `status` (the HTTP status code as a number), `reason` (the [HTTP reason phrase](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#name-status-codes)), `body` (the response body as a string) and, on DuckDB 2.0, `headers` (the response headers as a JSON object with lower-case names). A body that is not valid UTF-8 is returned base64-encoded with `"body_encoding": "base64"` (DuckDB 2.0).
description:
Issue an HTTP `GET` against `url` and return the response as JSON. Synchronous — DuckDB blocks until the response arrives or the request fails.

Extract fields from the result with DuckDB's JSON operators: `->>` for string fields, `->` for nested JSON. To dive into a JSON response body, cast it: `((http_get(...)->>'body')::JSON)->>'$.field'`.

For endpoints that need request headers (auth tokens, content negotiation) or query parameters, pass `headers` and `params`: both are `MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)`, and `params` is appended to the URL as a query string.

A request that gets no response (DNS failure, refused connection, timeout) returns `status` `-1` with the error message in `reason` rather than raising an error. HTTP error statuses (404, 500, ...) are returned as-is.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** requests go through DuckDB's own HTTP stack — `https://` and every method other than plain-HTTP `GET` use the [httpfs](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/overview) extension (autoloaded), so [`http_timeout`, `http_retries`, `http_proxy`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https) and [HTTP secrets](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https#authenticating) apply. Requests are refused when `enable_external_access` is false. Redirects are followed up to `http_client_max_redirects` (default 10) and re-checked on every hop: `https://` is never redirected to `http://`, and `Authorization`/`Cookie` headers are dropped when a redirect changes host. Bodies larger than `http_client_max_response_size` (default 100 MiB) raise an error.

examples.description: Send request headers and query parameters
Pull a field out of a JSON response body
Per-row enrichment against a REST API
examples.code:
SELECT u.id,
       u.email,
       ((http_get('https://api.example.com/score/' || u.id::VARCHAR)->>'body')::JSON)->>'$.score' AS score
FROM users u
WHERE u.last_seen > now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
LIMIT 100;

name: http_post

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Optional request headers as a [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map), e.g. `MAP{'accept': 'application/json'}`. Names and values containing line breaks are rejected. On DuckDB 2.0 the parameter can be left out (`NULL` means no headers).

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: **DuckDB 2.0.** The request body as `JSON`, sent with `Content-Type: application/json` unless `headers` sets another `Content-Type`. A `STRUCT` or `MAP` is converted to a JSON object. Optional: no body sends an empty POST.

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: The request body, under the name earlier builds used. Still accepted on DuckDB 2.0 as an alias for `body` (passing both is an error); it is the only name on the Haybarn 1.5 build.

description:
Issue an HTTP `POST` with a JSON request body. Use this for REST APIs that consume JSON. On DuckDB 2.0 the body parameter is named `body`; `params =>` keeps working, so the examples below run on both builds.

For `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies (older REST APIs, OAuth token endpoints, HTML form handlers), use `http_post_form` instead.

Keep credentials out of cached query plans by binding them through `SET VARIABLE` + `getenv`, or (DuckDB 2.0) store them in an HTTP secret — see Securing credentials.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** requests go through DuckDB's own HTTP stack — `https://` and every method other than plain-HTTP `GET` use the [httpfs](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/overview) extension (autoloaded), so [`http_timeout`, `http_retries`, `http_proxy`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https) and [HTTP secrets](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https#authenticating) apply. Requests are refused when `enable_external_access` is false. Redirects are followed up to `http_client_max_redirects` (default 10) and re-checked on every hop: `https://` is never redirected to `http://`, and `Authorization`/`Cookie` headers are dropped when a redirect changes host. Bodies larger than `http_client_max_response_size` (default 100 MiB) raise an error.

Read just the status to verify the call succeeded

name: http_post_form

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Optional request headers as a [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map), e.g. `MAP{'accept': 'application/json'}`. Names and values containing line breaks are rejected. On DuckDB 2.0 the parameter can be left out (`NULL` means no headers).

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Form fields as a `MAP`. Each entry is URL-encoded into the request body using [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1866).

description:
Issue an HTTP `POST` with the `params` map encoded as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` — the body shape used by HTML forms, many older REST APIs, and OAuth 2.0 token endpoints.

The extension sets the request's `Content-Type` header to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for you; you don't need to put it in `headers` manually.

For JSON request bodies, use `http_post` instead.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** requests go through DuckDB's own HTTP stack — `https://` and every method other than plain-HTTP `GET` use the [httpfs](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/overview) extension (autoloaded), so [`http_timeout`, `http_retries`, `http_proxy`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https) and [HTTP secrets](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https#authenticating) apply. Requests are refused when `enable_external_access` is false. Redirects are followed up to `http_client_max_redirects` (default 10) and re-checked on every hop: `https://` is never redirected to `http://`, and `Authorization`/`Cookie` headers are dropped when a redirect changes host. Bodies larger than `http_client_max_response_size` (default 100 MiB) raise an error.

name: http_head

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to issue the [`HEAD`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/HEAD) request against.

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Optional request headers as a [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map), e.g. `MAP{'accept': 'application/json'}`. Names and values containing line breaks are rejected. On DuckDB 2.0 the parameter can be left out (`NULL` means no headers).

returns: A JSON object with `status`, `reason` and `headers` — the response headers as a JSON object with lower-case names (repeated headers are joined with `, `). No body.
description:
Issue an HTTP `HEAD` request. Returns `{status, reason, headers}` and no body. Use it for liveness checks or to test whether a URL exists before fetching the full payload with `http_get`.

**Changed in the DuckDB 2.0 build:** `headers` is a JSON object (`res->'headers'->>'content-type'`). Earlier builds returned it as a JSON-encoded string; `(res->>'headers')::JSON` works on both.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** requests go through DuckDB's own HTTP stack — `https://` and every method other than plain-HTTP `GET` use the [httpfs](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/overview) extension (autoloaded), so [`http_timeout`, `http_retries`, `http_proxy`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https) and [HTTP secrets](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/httpfs/https#authenticating) apply. Requests are refused when `enable_external_access` is false. Redirects are followed up to `http_client_max_redirects` (default 10) and re-checked on every hop: `https://` is never redirected to `http://`, and `Authorization`/`Cookie` headers are dropped when a redirect changes host. Bodies larger than `http_client_max_response_size` (default 100 MiB) raise an error.
